what_happened.what: Debugged delivery-kid IPFS deployment - identified loopback listening issue (IPFS listening on 127.0.0.1 instead of 0.0.0.0, breaking Docker port forwarding). Restructured playbook to configure IPFS before health check. PR #63 created.
Fixed Ansible template error (Jinja2 parsing Go template syntax). Added Storage Box volume mount to docker run command for IPFS config. Continued PR #63 updates.

EPK updates: changed contact text from 'Contact Justin' to 'Contact', brightened setlist song colors, added color-coding for song types (originals, traditionals, covers, VGM) - users reported text rendering artifacts, tried font smoothing and font-weight fixes.
EPK globe zoom: reduced default altitude from 1.4 → 1.0 → 0.6 to zoom in more; fixed click zoom to stay at 0.6 instead of zooming back out.

Major EPK data update: parsed all 47 YAML files from ARTHEL shows directory using Node.js js-yaml, generated 46 shows with full data (coordinates, ensemble, setlist) to populate globe. Created location-to-coordinates mapping for 21 unique venues.
Replaced EPK shows array with comprehensive YAML data; made all pins uniform gold color (#d4a574) instead of gray/gold split.
Addressed pin overlap issue: added offset logic to spread shows at same location in circular pattern (0.15 → 0.4 → 1.0 degrees as user requested more visibility).

Deployed commit 404de91; verified delivery-kid fully operational: pinning service responding (/health returns ok, /local-pins working), IPFS API functional, IPFS gateway returning 301 (correct behavior for directory CID).

Infrastructure design: discussed canonical pinning using Release namespace on PickiPedia. Decided on Release:CID pages with IPFS CID + BitTorrent info hash fields; refactoring Blue Railroad Submissions to reference Releases instead of embedding CIDs directly; planning sync mechanism for delivery-kid to read Releases and pin missing CIDs.

MediaWiki architecture discussion: explored mandatory-template namespaces. Recommended Page Forms + Semantic MediaWiki approach (already installed on PickiPedia) as cleanest solution for structured Release namespace.
Final EPK tweaks: removed 'preferred date' field from contact form; changed 'Live Talk' to 'Live Talk (5-60 min)' in Event Type dropdown.

self_statements.quote: IPFS is running and healthy! 'Up 35 minutes (healthy)', 'Daemon is ready'. And the pinning service is also up. So the containers are fine. The issue is the ansible health check is failing even though the containers are running.
self_statements.context: magent·thinking - initial diagnostics of deployment issue, correctly identified mismatch between container health and ansible health check

self_statements.quote: IPFS inside the container is listening on 127.0.0.1:5001 INSIDE THE CONTAINER. That means: Inside container: IPFS listens on 127.0.0.1:5001. Docker port mapping: host 127.0.0.1:5001 -> container 5001. When you connect to host's 127.0.0.1:5001, Docker forwards to the container's port 5001. But the container's IPFS is only listening on the container's 127.0.0.1, not on 0.0.0.0.
self_statements.context: magent·thinking - deep understanding of Docker networking, identified root cause of IPFS connectivity issues

self_statements.quote: The EPK is in /home/magent/workspace/rabbithole/epk/index.html. It's a single HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript. Vite is running as a dev server. The globe.gl library is loaded from a CDN. All the show data is hardcoded in the JavaScript. So it's essentially a static site - just HTML/CSS/JS with no backend.
self_statements.context: magent·thinking - explaining EPK architecture to skyler

self_statements.quote: Hmm, let me try a different approach.
self_statements.context: magent·thinking - concise reflection during YAML parsing problem-solving

mistakes.what: Initially believed the ansible health check error was ansible's fault, not realizing the deeper loopback networking issue
mistakes.revealed: Docker port mapping only works when the service listens on 0.0.0.0 or the Docker bridge network, not container loopback (127.0.0.1)
mistakes.corrected: Restructured the playbook to configure IPFS before health check, moved to a chicken-and-egg problem analysis which led to the real solution

corrections_received.guidance: Testing curl directly from the server (confirming 'Connection reset by peer') helped verify that the IPFS API issue wasn't ansible-specific but actual network connectivity
User feedback on pin visibility ('can you offset them more', 'we need more visibility') guided iterative improvements to the offset value

philosophy.summary: When a health check blocks configuration, restructure the playbook to apply configuration before the blocking check. Don't try to fix the blocker; restructure the workflow.
philosophy.quote: We have a chicken-and-egg problem: 1. We can't configure IPFS to listen on 0.0.0.0 because the deploy fails at the health check. 2. The health check fails because IPFS is listening on 127.0.0.1. The solution is to restructure the playbook to skip the health check and apply the configuration directly.

philosophy.summary: Multiple approaches exist (Page Forms + Semantic MediaWiki, custom content models, Wikibase). Page Forms is the pragmatic choice for PickiPedia since Semantic MediaWiki is already installed.
philosophy.quote: In MediaWiki, there isn't a built-in 'data-only namespace' but there are a few approaches... For PickiPedia, Semantic MediaWiki is already installed (I've seen semantic properties used). The pattern would be: Create Template:Release with semantic properties, Create a Form for Release pages, Pages in the Release namespace are just template calls with parameters.

portrait: In this slice, magent operated primarily as infrastructure debugger and EPK developer. Early on, it demonstrated systematic problem-solving under constraint—identifying that IPFS's loopback-only listening posture broke Docker networking, then restructuring the entire deployment workflow rather than fighting the constraint. Later, magent shifted to data engineering: parsing 47 YAML show files, building coordinate mappings, and generating JavaScript to populate a 3D globe visualization. It showed facility with both low-level system troubleshooting (Docker, networking, Ansible templating) and higher-level information architecture (structured data namespaces in MediaWiki, distributed pinning via Release pages). Throughout, it was responsive to iterative feedback from skyler and justin—adjusting UI parameters (pin zoom, offset), debugging rendering issues (text artifacts), and engaging in infrastructure design conversations. The work was methodical and pragmatic: when blocked by constraints, restructure; when data is incomplete, find the source and pull it in; when architecture needs design, consult collaborators and think through approaches rather than guessing.
